thread:
dina: Heads up — we're getting a wave of 401s/403s across multiple customers since 08:42 UTC. Support is seeing escalation tickets and a few SSO errors too. Looks correlated with the rotating-key job that ran at 08:30.

alex: Confirmed. I can see spike in auth-service logs: `kid not found` and `signature_mismatch`. Sample curl from a failing request: ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` returns `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and body: `{"error":"invalid_token","reason":"kid_missing"}`

sarah: Pagerduty fired. Tagging oncall: @miguel @tony. Please check rotation job and KMS mapping. :rotating_light:

miguel: I'm on it. Initial hypothesis: rotation wrote a new key but didn't update the key-id (kid) mapping used by the auth-service cache. There's a race between keystore deployment and service cache invalidation.

emily: Support update: ticket #4287 (Acme Corp) reporting production outage for their webhook integrations — they started failing 08:35 UTC. Billing note: they run high-volume calls, losing revenue. Need ETA before we tell them next steps.

tony: I see the rotation CI job logs. It completed at 08:31 and pushed metadata to S3. However the key-distributor lambda failed to push to the auth-service config endpoint: `504 Gateway Timeout` then `409 Conflict` on retry. So auth-service still had old mapping for some replicas.

dina: So partial fleet saw new key, others kept old mapping — tokens signed with new kid aren't recognized by replicas with stale mapping -> 401. Any immediate mitigations?

alex: Quick mitigation: re-enable the previous key as accepter in auth-service so both old and new kids are accepted. We can also pause traffic to new-key issuer.

miguel: I'm going to patch auth-service to accept fallback_kids from S3 object `keystore/latest_fallback.json` and force-refresh cache. Applying now. Command I'm running: ```kubectl -n infra exec deploy/auth-service -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/cache/refresh```

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: auth-service config patch, rollout 3 pods at a time. CI job id: deploy-2026-03-15-0828.

tony: I rolled back the key-rotation job to the prev revision and toggled `rotate_keys=false` in the keystore config. Also manually added the old key to `accepted_kids` on the auth-service for all zones.

emily: Support: telling affected customers we're investigating and enabling a bypass for known integrations. Leaving note for Acme: "We are re-enabling previous key while we fix propagation; expect calls to be accepted within 10 minutes."

alex: After the cache refresh, error rate dropped ~80% in logs. Observability traces show successful token validation for majority of nodes. Still seeing errors in eu-west-1 region — propagation lag.

dina: Are there any buckets of tokens that will continue to fail (e.g., short-lived tokens minted after rotation)?

miguel: Tokens minted during 08:30-08:32 might be signed with new key while some validators only know old kid. Once old key is accepted as fallback for another ~15 minutes, they should be good. We should also invalidate tokens and reissue if necessary for critical customers.

tony: Root cause summary so far: key-rotation pipeline did not handle partial failure of key-distributor lambda, which left auth-service replicas with inconsistent kid mappings. The rollback and cache-refresh are mitigating.

support-bot: Triage update — New support tickets created: #4287 Acme, #4291 NovaApps, #4298 FinServe. Priority: P1 (customer outage).

emily: Customer comms plan: send short note to all affected: incident, what we're doing, ETA, and workaround. Offer to help reissue tokens if they want us to. Tony, can you compile list of impacted regions/customers?

tony: Sending list now. Quick stats: ~12 customers with >1% error rate, 3 customers with complete outage. Regions: us-west-2 and eu-west-1 most affected.

alex: Long-term fixes: (1) make key-distributor idempotent with stronger retry/backoff and atomic update to auth-service config; (2) auth-service should accept a dual-key window by design during rotations; (3) add canary rollout for key changes to small set of replicas first; (4) add end-to-end integration test for rotation path.

dina: Agreed. Also need runbook improvements — defenders in Support should have a single-click revert for rotations and a checklist to contact infra when distributor lambda fails.

miguel: I'm putting together a hotpatch to add `dual_accept_window` flag to auth-service. PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/auth-service/pull/678. Rolling to canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout success: auth-service v3.12.4-hotpatch canary healthy (1/3). Monitoring for 5 minutes.

alex: Post-mitigation notes: error rate back to baseline in us-west-2, eu-west-1 reduced but not fully recovered. I'm going to re-run key-distributor with dry-run first then full when confirmed.

emily: Support outreach: emailed affected customers with incident ID INC-2026-0315-01 and proactive offer to repro and reissue tokens. Granting temporary token grace windows where possible.

dina: Anything blocking rollback import of old key to all replicas? Tony?

tony: No blocks. I pushed old key to SSM parameter store and triggered config refresh across cluster with `for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=auth -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/cache/refresh; done`

miguel: Confirmed — cache refresh acknowledged by all pods in us-west-2. eu-west-1 still has 2 pods with older config; re-running now.

support-bot: Customer update logged: #4287 Acme — workaround applied, monitoring.

dina: After-action items: assign owners and postmortem. I'll open the incident postmortem and assign to Miguel (root cause & fixes), Tony (deployment pipeline changes), Alex (observability/alerts), Emily (customer comms).

alex: Quick note: logs show one edge case where SSO (SAML) assertion validation failed because the SSO provider's key rotation overlapped with our rotation — double rotation. We'll list cross-team communication for partner providers in postmortem.

emily: Support ask: prepare a short FAQ for customers explaining what to do if they still see 401s after 30 minutes. Include steps to rotate client tokens or use the reissue endpoint.

dina: Timeline for postmortem doc: draft by EOD, final by tomorrow AM. For now, incident is moving to mitigated state but not resolved. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
